extracted.intended_audience: graduate students / advanced undergraduates studying algebraic geometry (Math 216 students)
extracted.subtask_description: Chapter material and exercises defining and giving criteria, examples, and consequences of flatness for modules, sheaves, and morphisms of schemes. Emphasizes algebraic criteria (Tor, ideals), important examples, and geometric consequences (behavior under base change, fibers, cohomology).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: flat A-module
rubrics_metrics.description: An A-module M is flat if the functor M ⊗_A - is exact (equivalently, tensoring with M preserves all short exact sequences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the basic definition used throughout (see start of §24.2). Exercises use this to show basic properties and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples: free and projective modules are flat
rubrics_metrics.description: Free A-modules (even infinite rank) are flat. More generally, projective modules are flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as immediate examples and building blocks (Exercise 24.2.1(i) and references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization is flat
rubrics_metrics.description: If S is a multiplicative subset of B then the localization map B → S^{-1}B is a flat ring morphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to show many geometric maps (e.g., open immersions) are flat and for localization/stalk arguments (Exercise 1.6.F(a), 24.2.1(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flatness implies torsion-freeness / nonzerodivisor preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: If x is a non-zerodivisor of A and M is flat, then multiplication ×x : M → M is injective. In particular, flat modules are torsion-free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observation 24.2.2 gives this as a quick test for non-flatness and is used repeatedly in exercises and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flatness is local on primes/stalks
rubrics_metrics.description: An A-module M is flat iff M_p is a flat A_p-module for all prime ideals p (Proposition 24.2.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This justifies checking flatness on affine opens or stalks and extends to definitions for schemes and sheaves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: flat morphism of schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism of schemes π : X → Y is flat at p ∈ X if O_{X,p} is a flat O_{Y,π(p)}-module; π is flat if it is flat at all points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables translation of module-flatness criteria to morphisms; see Definitions 24.2.5–24.2.7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: flat quasicoherent sheaf over a base
rubrics_metrics.description: Given π : X → Y and a quasicoherent sheaf F on X, F is flat over Y at p if F_p is a flat O_{Y,π(p)}-module, and flat over Y if flat at all p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unifies the notions of flat sheaf and flat morphism (specialize X=Y or F=O_X).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitivity of flatness
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is a flat B-algebra and M is A-flat then M is B-flat (Exercise 24.2.D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard compositional property used in many arguments about base change and pushforward/pullback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flatness preserved by base change
rubrics_metrics.description: If M (or a quasicoherent sheaf F) is flat over a base, then its pullback under any base change is flat over the new base (Exercises 24.2.C and 24.2.I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key geometric property: products over a field are flat over their factors; used to analyze fibers and families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open embeddings are flat
rubrics_metrics.description: Open immersions give flat morphisms (Exercise 24.2.E).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic reality check/example for geometric intuitions about flat maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pullback of closed subschemes/ideal sheaves under flat maps agrees with scheme-theoretic pullback
rubrics_metrics.description: For a fibred product diagram, if β is flat then α^*(I_{V/X}) ≅ I_{Y×_Z V / W}; more generally if V is flat over Z then equality holds without hypotheses on β (24.2.9 and 24.3.H).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In words: pullback of ideal sheaves as quasicoherent sheaves agrees with pullback of closed subschemes under flatness; important for exactness of ideal sequence pullbacks and geometric reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flat maps send associated points to associated points
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is flat (locally Noetherian), then any associated point of X maps to an associated point of Y (Exercise 24.2.J).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to rule out flatness in examples by tracking associated primes; used to show many explicit morphisms are not flat (Exercise 24.2.K).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohomology commutes with flat base change
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a Cartesian square with f quasicompact and separated and g flat, for any quasicoherent F the natural maps g^*(R^i f_* F) → R^i f'_* (g'^* F) are isomorphisms (Theorem 24.2.8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important consequence: higher pushforwards and cohomology of quasicoherent sheaves behave well under flat base change; see Exercise 24.2.M for proof hints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pullback of effective Cartier divisors and regular embeddings via flat maps
rubrics_metrics.description: Under a flat morphism π : X → Y, pullback of an effective Cartier divisor remains an effective Cartier divisor; regular embeddings pull back to regular embeddings (Exercise 24.2.N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric preservation results often used in deformation and intersection-theoretic arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blowup commutes with flat base change
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is a morphism and Z ⊂ Y is a closed subscheme, then Bl_Z(Y) ×_Y X ≅ Bl_{Z×_Y X}(X) when appropriate flatness hypotheses hold (Exercise 24.2.P(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete compatibility statement for basic birational constructions under flat base change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideal-theoretic (Tor) criterion for flatness
rubrics_metrics.description: An A-module M is flat iff Tor^A_1(M, A/I) = 0 for every ideal I of A (Theorem 24.4.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This refines the Tor characterization: it suffices to test Tor_1 with quotients by ideals; foundational for many explicit checks and classifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equational criterion for flatness
rubrics_metrics.description: M is flat iff whenever a finite A-linear relation ∑ a_i m_i = 0 in M occurs, it can be expressed via a matrix factorization: there exist m'_j and a_{ij} in A with m_i = ∑ a_{ij} m'_j and ∑ a_i a_{ij} = 0 for all j (Exercise 24.4.A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete, elementwise criterion that is often used to show non-flatness by giving relations not explained by relations in A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suffices to check finitely generated ideals
rubrics_metrics.description: In Theorem 24.4.1 it suffices to check Tor_1(M, A/I)=0 for finitely generated ideals I (24.4.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical simplification: reduces infinite verifications to finitely generated cases using filtered colimits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flat = torsion-free over a PID
rubrics_metrics.description: For modules over a principal ideal domain, M is flat iff M is torsion-free (Exercise 24.4.B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to classify flat modules concretely in classical algebraic settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion over a DVR
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer t, then an A-module M is flat iff multiplication by t is injective on M (equivalently (M : t) = 0) (Exercise 24.4.C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives geometric intuition for flatness over regular curves and is used in many fiberwise flatness checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion over the dual numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: For A = k[t]/(t^2), M is flat iff multiplication by t induces an isomorphism M/tM → tM (Exercise 24.4.D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important in deformation theory; a hands-on test using the small ideal structure of dual numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finitely presented modules over local rings: flat ⇔ free ⇔ projective
rubrics_metrics.description: If (A,m) is a local ring and M is finitely presented, then M is flat iff M is free iff M is projective (Theorem 24.4.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key structural result; proof uses Nakayama and finite presentation hypotheses. Corollary: coherent sheaf on a scheme is flat iff locally free (24.4.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherent sheaf flat iff locally free
rubrics_metrics.description: A coherent sheaf F on X is flat over X iff it is locally free (Corollary 24.4.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric translation of the previous theorem, important for moduli and family arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite flat morphisms characterized by pushforward being locally free
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is finite, reduced and locally Noetherian hypotheses, then π is flat iff π_* O_X is locally free iff the rank function q ↦ dim_{κ(q)} (π_* O_X ⊗ κ(q)) is locally constant (Exercise 24.4.H).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a practical test for finite flatness and shows finite flat morphisms have locally constant degree (Exercise 24.4.G).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for flatness over a regular curve
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y with Y a regular (locally Noetherian) curve, then π is flat iff all associated points of X map to the generic point(s) of Y (Exercise 24.4.K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A useful geometric criterion specialized to one-dimensional bases; shows nontrivial maps from integral schemes to curves are flat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flat morphisms prevent jumping of fiber dimension
rubrics_metrics.description: For flat morphisms (in good situations) there is no jumping of fibre dimension — fiber-dimension behavior is controlled and does not 'jump' (foreshadowed in Exercise 24.2.K and Proposition 24.5.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to exclude non-flat examples (e.g., two planes meeting at a point) and to reason about constancy of dimensions in families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flatness and constancy of cohomological invariants in families
rubrics_metrics.description: In flat families (with appropriate hypotheses, e.g., projective and finitely presented), numerical invariants such as Euler characteristic, Hilbert polynomial, degree, arithmetic genus, and intersection numbers are constant in fibers (referenced for §24.7 and related exercises).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motivational geometric consequences of flatness used throughout the chapter; detailed statements/proofs given in §24.7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flat pullback preserves exactness of closed-subscheme sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Exact sequences cutting out closed subschemes (ideal-sheaf exact sequences) remain exact after flat pullback; this property is not only necessary but also sufficient for flatness in some formulations (see Theorem 24.4.1 discussion and 24.2.9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps visualize flatness as 'restricting nicely to closed subschemes' and is used in practical checks.
